name: loading-veil
description: A dim veil over one area with a small dark "Loading" tooltip: the area under it is loading. Show and hide with the hidden attribute.

props.name: scope
props.description: "page" makes the veil fixed over the whole viewport (a page's first load); omitted, it covers its positioned parent.

rationale: The veil covers its positioned parent (inset 0) above the content (z-index 5, below popups at 100 and toasts at 200) with the popup overlay color (bg.overlay) at 50% opacity, exactly like a popup's backdrop, so 'this area is busy' reads the same way as 'this area is behind a dialog'. The tooltip is a dark box (Figma base/900 with a base/1000 hairline, white text, 10px padding and gap) holding the spinner glyph (a CSS mask, so it takes the text color) and the label. It is centered horizontally and translated -50% / -50%, so the host places its center by setting style.top (Figma draws it at the middle of the window, not of the area). Not sourced from Figma: the hidden-attribute API and role="status". Rendering verified in light and dark themes. The spinner rotates clockwise, 1.2s linear per turn, and stops under prefers-reduced-motion. scope="page" fixes the veil to the viewport (z-index 50, tooltip at 50%) so any dashboard page can show a first-load state.
a11y_notes: role="status" so the loading message is announced when the veil is shown; the spinner is aria-hidden. The veil does not trap focus: the host should also mark the area inert while loading if it must not be used.
